Current Psychology
https://doi.org/10.1007/s12144-022-03573-2

A meta‑analysis of the weight of advice in decision‑making
Phoebe E. Bailey1 · Tarren Leon1 · Natalie C. Ebner2 · Ahmed A. Moustafa3 · Gabrielle Weidemann4
Accepted: 26 July 2022
© The Author(s) 2022

Abstract
The degree to which people take advice, and the factors that influence advice-taking, are of broad interest to laypersons,
professionals, and policy-makers. This meta-analysis on 346 effect sizes from 129 independent datasets (N = 17, 296)
assessed the weight of advice in the judge-advisor system paradigm, as well as the influence of sample and task characteristics. Information about the advisor(s) that is suggestive of advice quality was the only unique predictor of the overall pooled
weight of advice. Individuals adjusted estimates by 32%, 37%, and 48% in response to advisors described in ways that suggest low, neutral, or high quality advice, respectively. This indicates that the benefits of compromise and averaging may be
lost if accurate advice is perceived to be low quality, or too much weight is given to inaccurate advice that is perceived to
be high quality. When examining the three levels of perceived quality separately, advice-taking was greater for subjective
and uncertain estimates, relative to objective estimates, when information about the advisor was neutral in terms of advice
quality. Sample characteristics had no effect on advice-taking, thus providing no evidence that age, gender, or individualism
influence the weight of advice. The findings contribute to current theoretical debates and provide direction for future research.
Keywords Advice-taking · Estimation · Meta-analysis · Egocentric discounting · Decision-making
The definition and measurement of advice varies across disciplines and research paradigms (MacGeorge & Van Swol,
2018a). It has been suggested that advice may be a higherorder factor subsuming lower-order factors, including, but
not limited to, provision for or against a specific recommendation, and provision of guidance on how to make a decision (Bonaccio & Dalal, 2006). The current meta-analysis
synthesises studies using the judge–advisor system (JAS)
paradigm (Sniezek & Buckley, 1995), which is the most
commonly applied measure of advice-taking. In this paradigm, the judge is asked to provide a numerical estimate
(e.g., distance between two cities) before receiving an advisor’s (or advisors’) estimate(s). Then the judge is invited to
revise their estimate, and sometimes an incentive is provided

Abstract A major problem that resulted from the massive use of social media networks is the diffusion of incorrect information. However, very few studies have investigated the impact of incorrect information on individual and collective decisions. We performed experiments in which participants had to estimate a series of quantities twice, before and after receiving some social information. Unbeknownst to the participants, we controlled the degree of inaccuracy of the social information through “virtual influencers” that provided some incorrect information. We find that incorrect social information does not necessarily impair the collective wisdom of groups and can even help a group perform better when it overestimates the true value, by partly compensating a human underestimation bias. I found information about the "Wise Teamwork" paper by Silver, Mellers, and Tetlock. Here's what I found:

"Wise Teamwork: Collective confidence calibration predicts the effectiveness of group discussion" was published by Silver, Mellers, and Tetlock in 2021 in the Journal of Experimental Social Psychology, Volume 96.

The research involved two large laboratory studies that explored the effects of 969 face-to-face discussions on the judgment accuracy of 211 teams facing a range of numeric estimation problems from geographic distances to historical dates to stock prices.

Although participants nearly always expected discussions to make their answers more accurate, the actual effects of group interaction on judgment accuracy were decidedly mixed. Importantly, a novel, group-level measure of collective confidence calibration robustly predicted when discussion helped or hurt accuracy.

# Individuals, Crowds, and the Network Dynamics of Belief Accuracy

Supporting code and data for the publication Pilgrim, C., Becker, J., "Individuals, Crowds, and the Network Dynamics of Belief Accuracy".

## Theoretical

The Theoretical folder contains code for the main equations presented in the paper. These are rigorously tested against simulations of DeGroot updating. 

The plots folder contains the code to replicate the theoretical plots.

content.text:
Of the 14 requested items, 9 have data under an explicit repository licence. Four more licensed datasets turned up in the extra search. The rest are excluded, not yet public, or unverified. No data files were opened.

**Method note:** one Europe PMC call started downloading a supplementary-files zip for the Jayles 2017 paper (PMC5703270). I stopped it within 2 minutes and deleted the partial file unopened. Nothing was listed or read from it. OpenAlex was not needed.

### Requested datasets

| # | Dataset | Repository | Licence on record | Contents (from README, codebook or paper) | How verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Becker, Brackbill & Centola 2017 | PNAS SI Dataset S1 (`pnas.1615978114.sd01.csv`) only. No repository deposit. | **UNVERIFIED / not openly licensed.** The article is under standard PNAS terms, not CC (Europe PMC shows no licence). | 1,360 participants; 59 tasks; 3 rounds (response_1–3); true values known; decentralized, centralized and solo conditions | PMC text; Becker's loader scripts; Dataverse search found no deposit |
| 2 | Becker, Porter & Centola 2019 | Harvard Dataverse [10.7910/DVN/OE6UMR](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/OE6UMR). Mirror: github.com/joshua-a-becker/wisdom-of-partisan-crowds | **CC0 1.0** on Dataverse (Dataverse default). The GitHub mirror has no licence. | "Supplementary Dataset.csv" = all trial data; 2 experiments; partisan factual questions answered before and after seeing peers' estimates. Participant and question counts not checked (PMC blocked by captcha). | Dataverse API; GitHub README |
| 3 | Lorenz et al. 2011 | PNAS SI `sd01.xls` only | **UNVERIFIED / not openly licensed.** "PNAS open access option" means free to read, not a CC licence. | 144 participants; 12 sessions × 12; 6 questions; 5 rounds (E1–E5); true values known | PMC text; Becker's loader script |
| 4 | Jayles et al. 2017 | None | **EXCLUDED: no dataset deposited.** The article is CC BY-NC-ND, but the SI is only an appendix PDF. | 29 questions; 5,394 × 2 estimates (before and after social information); true values known | Europe PMC article XML lists only `sapp.pdf` |
| 5 | Kao et al. 2018 | Royal Society figshare: 10.6084/m9.figshare.6120665, 6120674, 6120677, 6120680, 6120683, plus readme 6120671 | **CC BY 4.0** on every figshare record. The article itself says "All rights reserved"; the repository record governs. | One jar per participant. Most files are a single column of estimates. The 659-object file has initial guess, social group size N, social information shown, second guess, times and demographics (602 participants). | figshare API; 1.3 KB readme text read |
| 6 | Almaatouq et al. 2020 | Harvard Dataverse [10.7910/DVN/EOYZKH](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/EOYZKH) | **CC0 1.0** (Dataverse default) | `all_studies_round_data.tab` and `game_data.tab`; 2 experiments (N=719 and N=702); groups of 12; 20 correlation-guessing rounds with pre- and post-influence estimates; true values known | Dataverse API; data statement in article XML |
| 7 | Becker, Guilbeault & Smith 2022 | Harvard Dataverse [10.7910/DVN/ZNMISU](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/ZNMISU) | **CC0 1.0** (Dataverse default) | Main experiment and pilot are **binary** classification data. Also contains `gurcay_data.tab`, a third-party redeposit of Gürçay 2015 (est1, est2, true values); the depositor may not hold the rights. The pooled numeric analysis fetches Becker 2017 and Lorenz 2011 from PNAS at run time, so those two are **not** in the deposit and not covered by CC0. | Dataverse API; README and loader script read |
| 9 | Wulff, Mergenthaler-Canseco & Hertwig 2018 | Zenodo [10.5281/zenodo.1491449](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1491449) (latest version) | **CC-BY-SA-4.0** (share-alike) | Data from 28 publications. Zip contents from the Zenodo preview: README.txt, VariableNames.pdf, cho.txt, des.txt, exp.txt (407.6 MB), pro.txt. exp.txt is probably the sample sequences; this cannot be confirmed without opening the zip. | Zenodo API and preview listing |
| 10 | CPC15 (Erev et al. 2017) | Zenodo [10.5281/zenodo.321652](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.321652) | **CC BY 4.0** | More than 330k choices; 3 experiment CSVs | Zenodo API (latest version) |
| 10 | CPC18 (Plonsky et al.) | Zenodo [10.5281/zenodo.2571510](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.2571510) (full) and [845873](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.845873) (calibration set) | **CC BY 4.0** | 694,500 choices; risk, ambiguity and experience-with-feedback tasks; PDF data dictionary | Zenodo API (latest version) |
| 11 | Technion Prediction Tournament (Erev et al. 2010) | Defunct page tx.technion.ac.il/~erev/Comp (Wayback snapshot from 2017 has "Raw Data" pages) | **EXCLUDED: no licence** | Description, E-sampling and E-repeated conditions; estimation and competition sets | Archived page text |
| 12 | Jaquiery & Yeung, date-estimation judge–advisor tasks | OSF [osf.io/h254u](https://osf.io/h254u), components fsgnb/zpk82, j3kdh/qb4nz, s3tk9/f5ny9 | **CC-By Attribution 4.0 International** on the parent and every data component | Trial-level `AdvisedTrial.csv` files with advisor advice, confidence, correct answer and responses; data dictionaries included | OSF API node walk; data dictionary read |
| 12 | Rebholz, Groß & Röseler (anchoring, advice-taking and hindsight reliability) | OSF [osf.io/4n3am](https://osf.io/4n3am) | **CC-By 4.0** | Study 1 `reliabilities.csv` is compiled from other open datasets (2.7 MB). Level of detail not checked. | OSF API |
| 12 | Excluded advice-taking datasets | Schultze precision osf.io/jgmd6; Schultze sampling osf.io/6xe5h; Bailey et al. 2022 weight-of-advice meta-analysis osf.io/atz6y | jgmd6 and 6xe5h: **EXCLUDED, no licence.** atz6y: **EXCLUDED, private view-only link, effect sizes only.** | – | OSF API |
| 13 | van Dolder & van den Assem 2018 | None | **EXCLUDED: proprietary.** Holland Casino data under NDA, not public. | 1.2M guesses | Data statement in author PDF |
| 13 | Steegen et al. 2014 | OSF [osf.io/ivfu6](https://osf.io/ivfu6), data component arxvg | **EXCLUDED: no licence** on the parent or any of its 6 components. No other deposit found on Zenodo, Dataverse or OSF search. | Raw data for immediate and delayed conditions (2 sessions) | OSF API walk |
| 13 | Herzog & Hertwig | None found | **UNVERIFIED / none found** | – | OSF (SHARE) search |
| 13 | Other inner-crowd projects | osf.io/b3f6d, qsxp8, s3quz, ja3xg: no licence. osf.io/fsjru (Efendić & van de Calseyde) is **CC0 1.0** but has no files in storage; only registrations 4agxj, c7vjf and a8deh exist, and these were not checked. | Excluded (fsjru unverified) | – | OSF API |
| 14 | Thomas et al. 2019 (GLAM) | GitHub [glamlab/gaze-bias-differences](https://github.com/glamlab/gaze-bias-differences) | **MIT** on the repo | Preprocessed trial-level choice, response time and gaze CSVs for Krajbich 2010, Krajbich 2011, Tavares 2017 and Folke 2016 (Folke is separately CC BY 4.0 on figshare) | `gh api` licence check; README; the paper's data statement points to this repo |
| 14 | Krajbich et al. 2010 | Only as the preprocessed copy in the GLAM repo above (MIT). Krajbich co-authored Thomas et al. 2019. | Covered by the GLAM repo's MIT licence | – | As above |

### Extra datasets (item 8)

| Dataset | Repository | Licence | Contents | How verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jayles, Sire & Kurvers 2021, RSIF, full vs averaged social information | figshare [10.6084/m9.figshare.12529571](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.12529571) | **CC BY 4.0** | Participant × question rows: true value, personal estimate, second estimate, all estimates shown as social information, treatment | figshare API |
| Jayles et al. 2021, PLOS Comp Biol, "Crowd control" | figshare [12472034](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.12472034) | **CC BY 4.0** | Same layout, plus flag for questions reused from earlier studies | figshare API |
| Jayles et al. 2020, RSIF, incorrect social information | figshare [12522527](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.12522527) and [11903421](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.11903421) | **CC BY 4.0** | Personal estimate, social information (geometric mean), second estimate, true value, share of virtual influencers | figshare API |
| DfE-DB (Yang, Spektor, Thoma, Hertwig & Wulff), 3.8M decisions-from-experience trials | GitHub dwulff/DfE-DB | Repo is **CC-BY-SA-4.0**, but **data not yet public**. README says release on acceptance; the data folders hold only processing scripts and READMEs. | – | `gh api` |
| Excluded: Navajas et al. 2018 | Copy in Becker's GitHub repo (`Data-Reanalyses`) | **EXCLUDED, no licence**; no data statement found | – | GitHub; arXiv PDF |
| Excluded: Almaatouq et al. 2021 task-dependence (pools 4 experiments) | OSF osf.io/xhn4r (CC-BY 4.0) holds only the PDF; data are in github.com/amaatouq/task-dependence | **EXCLUDED, GitHub repo has no licence** | – | OSF API; `gh api` |
| Excluded: Pilgrim & Becker 2024 (reanalyses 6 datasets) | github.com/chasmani/Individuals-Crowds-Network-Dynamics | **EXCLUDED, no licence** | – | `gh api` |
| Silver, Mellers & Tetlock 2021 | No deposit found; journal page paywalled | **UNVERIFIED** | – | Web search |

### Needs your decision
- **Dataverse CC0 is the platform default** (Becker 2019, Almaatouq 2020, Becker 2022). It is still an explicit licence on the record, so I counted it.
- **Two items use share-alike (CC-BY-SA-4.0):** the Wulff 2018 Zenodo data and the DfE-DB repo. Share-alike obliges any redistributed derivatives to carry the same licence.
- **Only the Kao 2018 and Jayles figshare datasets give a single social-information value shown before a revised estimate.** For pre- and post-influence estimates with a licence, the usable sources are Almaatouq 2020, Becker 2019, the redeposited Gürçay data (with the rights caveat), Kao 2018 and the Jayles figshare datasets.

Scratch scripts and metadata JSON are in /tmp/jdmsim as `scratch_licences_woc_*`. The Navajas, van Dolder and Pilgrim–Becker paper PDFs were also saved there under that prefix.
